title: Company accounts
examples: Where exactly do I find the total equity figure on the balance sheet?
If a company pays dividends, does that reduce the share capital or the reserves?
What is the difference between retained earnings and reserves?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the equity section of company accounts.
Share capital represents the money raised by issuing shares to investors.

draw.text: Share Capital: Money from selling shares

explain.say: Reserves are profits kept within the company for future use or expansion.

draw.text: Reserves: Profits kept for the business

explain.say: Dividends are payments made to shareholders from the company's profits.
The total equity is calculated by adding share capital and reserves, then subtracting dividends.
In real life, when a company expands, they might use reserves instead of issuing new shares.

faq.q: What is the difference between reserves and retained earnings?
faq.a: Retained earnings are the profits kept back, while reserves are specific amounts set aside for particular purposes.
asks: Are reserves the same as retained earnings?
Where do I see the difference between these two figures?

faq.q: Does paying dividends affect the share capital?
faq.a: No, paying dividends only reduces the total equity through the reserves, it does not change the amount of share capital.
asks: If dividends are paid, does share capital go down?
Is the reduction in equity always due to dividends?

faq.q: How is the total equity calculated?
faq.a: You add the share capital and the reserves, and then you subtract any dividends paid to find the total equity.
asks: What is the formula for total equity?
Can I calculate total equity without knowing the dividends?

faq.q: Can a company use its reserves to pay dividends?
faq.a: Yes, companies often use accumulated reserves to pay dividends when they have not made recent profits.
asks: Must a company have current profits to pay dividends?
What happens if reserves are used up paying dividends?

faq.q: What is the difference between paid-up and issued capital?
faq.a: Issued capital is the total shares offered, while paid-up capital is the actual money the company has received for those shares.
asks: Are issued and paid-up capital always the same?
Which figure is more important for the equity section?

facts: Share capital represents funds directly invested by shareholders.
Reserves are profits that have been kept within the company.
Dividends are distributions of company profits to its owners.
Total Equity = Share Capital + Reserves - Dividends (if applicable)

quiz.say: A company has a share capital of 50,000 and reserves of 30,000. If no dividends were paid, what is the total equity?
quiz.why: You add the share capital and the reserves together to find the total equity.

wrong.1: This only uses the share capital, forgetting the accumulated reserves.
wrong.2: This only uses the reserves, ignoring the initial investment from shareholders.
wrong.3: This incorrectly subtracts the two figures, which is not the required calculation.

quiz.say: If a company has Share Capital of 100,000, Reserves of 40,000, and pays 10,000 in dividends, what is the total equity?
quiz.why: You add the share capital and reserves, and then subtract the amount paid out as dividends.

wrong.0: This only calculates Reserves minus Dividends, ignoring the share capital.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds all three figures together.
wrong.3: This incorrectly assumes dividends reduce the share capital instead of the total equity.
